title: APOLLOS: GIFTED YET GUIDED
mv: I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
mvp: “I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.”1 Corinthians 3:6
assignment: Mention five (5) biblical characters who listened to instruction and support your answers with a Bible reference (2x5=10 marks).

b.x: Apollos was not among the most famous apostles, but his life carries remarkable lessons for believers today. Born in Alexandria, he was eloquent, knowledgeable, and fervent in spirit (Acts 18:24). Despite his brilliance, he humbly accepted correction from Aquila and Priscilla. His story highlights the balance between natural gifts and teachability, a quality needed in today’s gifted believers.

Apollos was an eloquent and knowledgeable man who communicated truth with clarity. He studied deeply and was mighty in the Scriptures (Acts 18:24); Fervent in Spirit, he was passionate and zealous in ministry (Acts 18:25); A courageous witness who boldly preached Christ and defended the faith (Acts 18:26, 28).
He, however, had incomplete knowledge, because he only knew the baptism of John (Acts 18:25). His brilliance caused division unintentionally (1 Corinthians 3:4-6).

Apollos submitted to Aquila and Priscilla’s mentorship: everyone, even skilled leaders and gifted ones, needs mentorship and feedback (Acts 18:26; Mark 8:27-28). Learn from others because, no matter how good you are, you cannot know it all. He embraced new knowledge: continuous and lifelong learning, keeps a leader relevant (Proverbs 9:9; 2 Timothy 2:15). He collaborated with Paul for souls rather than unfruitful competition: no matter your knowledge and eloquence, avoid arrogance, embrace teamwork and humility (1 Corinthians 3:6, 9; Ecclesiastes 4:9-10). He balanced passion with wisdom: effective people channel passion wisely (Proverbs 19:2; James 3:13).
Apollos was eloquent, passionate, and knowledgeable, yet, humble enough to be corrected. True greatness is not in talent alone, but also in a teachable spirit and teamwork.

i: Mention at least two areas of Apollos’ strength and weakness.
State four lessons believers can learn from Apollos.
